steps.what: Monitor maternal condition, vital signs and uterine contractions and perform physical examinations

tasks.design: Retain direct maternal monitoring and examination with the midwife. Existing maternity monitoring equipment in {OTHER} supports observation without replacing examination or clinical interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task requires direct observation of a changing person and interpretation of physical findings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing devices already support monitoring; no new clinical automation gain is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: A device reading can be incomplete, unreliable or inconsistent with the woman's presentation.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate observations, examination, communication and clinical context.
tasks.altitude: Clinical responsibility and bedside time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate assessment when findings need escalation
reach.learn: Clear clinical handover and uncertainty communication

evidence.claim: Maternal observation and physical examination remain human clinical work; registry and documentation tools in the digest do not establish bedside monitoring savings.

assumptions: Boundary is maternal monitoring and examination, not separate documentation automation or subsequent treatment. Existing care-team work stays outside and unchanged.

OTHER means maternity monitoring equipment. Midwife obtains patient/episode identity, current observations, timestamps, units, device context and examination findings during retained100 hours. Patient reports arise during the encounter before interpretation. No pre-existing normal-condition flag is assumed; missing or suspect measurements require direct clinical checking under existing practice.
Use native monitoring and record access before custom tools. Existing continuous-device runtime earns no new human time saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because the monitoring process and tools are unchanged.
unknowns: Clinical setting and available monitoring equipment
research_questions: Which monitoring minutes involve direct assessment that device display cannot replace?

tasks.short: Identify concerning pregnancy findings and refer

steps.what: Assess findings for tubal or ectopic pregnancies within professional responsibilities
Refer patients for appropriate assessment or treatments and communicate clinical uncertainty

tasks.design: Keep recognition, assessment and referral with the midwife using original clinical material in {DOCS} and direct {TELEPHONY} handover. No automated diagnostic or referral-urgency decision is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagnosis and appropriate referral depend on current clinical findings, scope and uncertainty.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record access and referral channels support care; no new diagnostic breakthrough is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Available findings may be incomplete or change after the initial assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise concern, communicate uncertainty and coordinate appropriate care without overstating a diagnosis.
tasks.altitude: Clinical decision rights and referral time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Concise handover of findings and uncertainties

evidence.claim: Pregnancy assessment and referral remain human clinical work; documentation and coding capabilities in the digest do not establish diagnostic savings.

assumptions: Boundary is midwife assessment and referral within existing professional scope, not independent specialist diagnosis or downstream treatment. Existing receiving-clinician work remains outside and unchanged.

Patient and existing clinical services produce the history and any available test reports before each related assessment; unavailable tests are not assumed completed. Midwife verifies patient/episode, report dates/versions, symptoms, findings and uncertainty during s1's70 hours and rechecks current condition during s2's30. Missing evidence prompts existing clinical assessment/referral practice, not a generated ectopic-pregnancy or urgency flag.
Retain native record access and referral channels before custom tools; no new structured capture task is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because the care process and tools are unchanged.
unknowns: Local professional scope and referral pathways
Available clinical services and existing test access
research_questions: Are assessment and referral minutes separated from subsequent specialist treatment time?

approvals.approved_version: Exact referral findings, uncertainty, current condition, destination and handover content; changes require fresh clinical check

steps.what: Conduct ongoing prenatal health assessments and track physical and emotional health changes

tasks.design: Retain prenatal assessment and discussion with the midwife using prior records in {DOCS}. A historical record supports comparison without replacing the current physical or emotional assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Health changes require direct assessment and a relationship in which concerns can be expressed.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support comparison; no new clinical assessment automation is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: A recorded value may not reflect current wellbeing or an unspoken concern.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise changes in context and invite sensitive information without reducing it to a score.
tasks.altitude: Prenatal care time and clinical responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate follow-up for changing prenatal needs

evidence.claim: Ongoing prenatal assessment remains human care; the digest's practice-statistics and note-drafting tools do not establish shorter physical/emotional assessments.

assumptions: Boundary is current and longitudinal clinical assessment, excluding separate registry statistics or report generation. Other care-team work remains outside and unchanged.

Prior care staff produce existing observations before the current encounter; patient produces current reports during it. Midwife checks identity, observation dates, source versions, findings and changes within retained100 hours. No free current-wellbeing, normal-change or reliable-history flag is assumed; gaps require direct clarification.
Native longitudinal record access precedes custom tools; no new automated score or capture duty is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because care and tools remain unchanged.
unknowns: Record completeness and patient support needs
research_questions: Which important changes emerge only through current examination and conversation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Current prenatal assessment and sensitive discussion retain time even with accessible prior records.

tasks.short: Establish and follow emergency contingency plans

steps.what: Establish emergency or contingency plans for mothers and newborns in the current care context
Approve current clinical actions and follow emergency or contingency plans as conditions evolve

tasks.design: Retain contextual planning and clinical response with the midwife, supported by approved {DOCS} protocols and {TELEPHONY} coordination. A plan does not replace current assessment or authorise automatic clinical action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Emergency response depends on evolving conditions and available care resources.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing protocols and communications support action; no new autonomous response is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: An appropriate earlier plan may need adaptation as circumstances change.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the plan no longer fits and coordinate a timely clinical response.
tasks.altitude: Planning, response time and clinical authority remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Emergency planning and response remain human clinical work; the digest does not establish automation savings for birth care.

assumptions: Boundary is focal midwife contingency planning and response, not specialist treatment or other staff execution. Existing team participation remains outside and unchanged.

Midwife verifies patient context, protocol version, care contacts/resources and relevant contingencies within s1's35 hours. Current observations arise before each action during s2; response observations arise after related action before reassessment. S2's65 hours include current-condition checks, decision and coordination. No free emergency-state, resource-ready or successful-response flag is assumed; uncertainty follows existing clinical escalation.
Retain native protocol access and communications before custom tools; approval is a clinical decision within the response, not a new administrative waiting stage.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool, model or care process is introduced.
unknowns: Existing clinical protocols and delegated roles
Available emergency resources and handover routes
